subject.name: Ethereum Name Service (ENS)
subject.one_line: ENS is an Ethereum naming protocol with registration and lookup contracts, user apps, and DAO governance supported by ENS Labs.

summary.text: ENS is an Ethereum naming protocol that maps readable names to addresses and other records, according to its documentation.
People register names through the ENS App and inspect them in ENS Explorer, according to ENS.
Yearly base prices run from $8 to $640 by name length, plus network fees, according to ENS.
The newer registration system launched in October 2026, according to ENS’s announcement.
The project’s contracts issue ownership tokens, ENS tokens enable voting, and optional art cards mark the upgrade, the project says.
Registration fees reach its Endowment, while treasury policy funds development and public goods, the project says.
Nick Johnson founded ENS, according to ENS’s YouTube channel.
ENS Labs develops the software, and the DAO governs the protocol and treasury, according to ENS.
The DAO wallet owns the newer registrar, while a council wallet administers part of lookup, according to chain readings.

lines.text: The ens.eth text records point to the ENS website, project X account and GitHub organization.

rerun.decode: Read registry.resolver(namehash("ens.eth")), then text(node,key) on that resolver. Decode the dynamic ABI strings. Handles map to x.com/ensdomains and github.com/ensdomains.

lines.text: The v2 root and registrar both point to the same .eth registry.

rerun.decode: Decode root.getSubregistry("eth") and registrar.ETH_REGISTRY() as addresses; compare them.

lines.text: The v2 registrar reports a minimum commitment age of 60 seconds.

rerun.decode: Decode MIN_COMMITMENT_AGE() as uint64; this is a configured minimum, not a transaction timing test.

lines.text: The public name lookup proxy routes through an intermediate proxy to the documented v2 resolver.

rerun.decode: Read implementation() on the public proxy, then on the returned intermediate proxy; compare the final address to the documented UniversalResolverV2 deployment.

lines.text: The v2 .eth owner is a one-signature Safe whose sole owner is the DAO wallet.

rerun.decode: Decode root.findOwner("eth") as address; on that Safe decode getThreshold() as uint256 and getOwners() as address[]. This does not enumerate Safe modules.

lines.text: The commemorative contract reports the name ENS Commemorative and the symbol ENSC.

rerun.decode: Decode name() and symbol() as dynamic ABI strings. The official app configuration identifies this deployment.

lines.text: The commemorative token has an owner wallet separate from the DAO wallet.

rerun.decode: Decode owner() as address and compare with the DAO wallet in A2. The controller of this wallet was not identified.

lines.text: The public name lookup proxy reports the DAO wallet as its administrator.

rerun.decode: Decode admin() as address.

lines.text: The intermediate name lookup proxy is administered by a five-of-eight council Safe.

rerun.decode: Decode admin() as address, then the returned Safe’s getThreshold() and getOwners(); count eight owners. This reads signer settings, not module permissions.

lines.text: The Endowment Safe reports one owner and a one-signature threshold.

rerun.decode: Decode getThreshold() and getOwners() on the Endowment Safe. Its sole owner is another address; modules and ultimate control are not established here.

lines.text: The v2 .eth registry grants its registrar registration and renewal roles.

rerun.decode: Decode hasRootRoles(65537,registrar) as bool. The published role library defines registration as bit 0 and renewal as bit 16.

differs.why: A deployment guide still describes registrations through version 1 pending launch; ENS announced version 2 live and the old controllers are disabled.

open_questions: When will ENS update the deployment guide to reflect the version 2 launch?
What is the complete effective control path for version 2 registries, lookup proxies, migration controllers and Safe modules?
Who controls the commemorative collection owner wallet 0xfbe6ce2d739df7077f407f6099ac804a076a760b?
What are the live supplies of ENSC and each name token family?
What will a particular name cost for a visitor at checkout, including gas and any expiry premium?
Does holding ENS confer any direct revenue entitlement beyond governance?
notes: This run fetched and hashed the instruction file, then fetched both earlier records in full. All earlier line origins are carried; repeated meanings were merged into one line and no earlier line was dropped. The specified registry remains marked main because it is the requested anchor and the legacy lookup directory, while newer registration and lookup contracts are listed separately. On November 23, 2026, the ENS homepage and pricing documentation still described version 2 as live. A fresh finalized Ethereum block was used to replay 56 proof calls; other proof readings retain their earlier pinned blocks and rerun instructions. Outside sources reviewed across the two records include Ethereum.org, GoDaddy, PayPal, ENS.Tools, The Block, The Defiant, ENSWhois, Blockscout, Anticapture and DefiLlama. The Size row uses a dated DefiLlama seven-day revenue figure; other trackers use different metrics and coverage. Name prices are examples or published base rates, not checkout offers. ENSC and name-token aggregate supplies were not established. The ENS documentation showed an AI-directed navigation prompt; it was treated as page data and not followed. The square favicon was fetched from the project domain. Local integrity checks and RPC replay are author checks, not independent review.
